caption: The drawing depicts a highly detailed wrought-iron gate and fence, labeled “The Cornstalk Fence.” The central feature is a rectangular gate that measures 45 inches wide, with intricate corn stalk motifs making up the vertical bars and horizontal sections of the gate and fence. The corn stalks have detailed leaves and ears of corn. On either side of the gate are fence posts topped with sculpted corn motifs resembling ears of corn with husks, positioned vertically. At the bottom of the posts are ornate bases featuring rounded, bulbous designs. The fence on both sides of the gate shows repeated stalk and leaf patterns. In the upper left and right corners of the drawing, additional detailed views are presented: on the left, a post measuring 75 inches in height, and on the right, a panel that is 80 inches tall and 57 inches wide. The entire composition is monochromatic, rendered in sepia-toned ink (likely a scanned or photographed drawing), with all lines and shading done in the same color. The style is technical and decorative, with a focus on line work and botanical ornamentation. Measurements are indicated with dashed lines and numbers. The whole drawing is set within a rectangular frame with rounded corners, and the label at the bottom is written in a script and serif font combination.
title: Cast Iron Gate and Fence
